dedupe_keys.name: agricultural health study ahs cohort of farmers and spouses

description: The Agricultural Health Study (AHS) is a long-running prospective cohort that studies how agricultural, lifestyle and genetic factors affect the health of farming populations, with recent topics such as drinking water quality and inflammatory bowel disease. More than 89,000 farmers and their spouses in Iowa and North Carolina have taken part since 1993, with a fourth cohort-wide follow-up described in the 2024 study update. It is funded by the National Cancer Institute and the National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences, with earlier roles for the Environmental Protection Agency and the National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health. Coverage is farmers and their spouses in the two states. Questionnaires are published and the data are available on request to researchers through collaboration with the study under its policies and process; no fee is stated. Caveats: participant data are confidential and not open, and the cohort covers only two states. For simulation it provides exposure and health outcome evidence to parameterise models of how chemical use and water contamination in farming regions affect health, a dimension of environmental impact assessments of agricultural infrastructure. It is related to the EPA National Emissions Inventory record in this catalogue, another exposure data source.
